title: The Mapmaker's Ridge
story:
From up here, the town was not an overwhelming tangle of clanking motor-carriages and unfamiliar alleys. From up here, the town was a quiet patchwork of mossy terracotta roofs, silver canals, and verdant courtyards. From up here, the world seemed to pause and breathe, suspended between the clearing morning mist and the promised highland rain. Barnaby rested his hands upon the cool stone balustrade, gazing out with the quiet contentment of someone who knew every chime and cobblestone by heart.

James reached to his leather chest strap, feeling the weight of his gathered treasures. He held up his green sea-glass for a fleeting second, watching Oakhaven turn into an emerald canopy that faintly echoed his old forest home. But when he lowered it, he found he loved the true colors just as much. Tracing the lines of the streets below, he recognized the winding ribbon of the Grand Canal where Silas's barge had drifted, the wide flagstones of the plaza where Mateo's loom clicked, and the tiny blue speck of Sofia and Rosa's courtyard tucked among the gardens.

With deliberate, careful hands, James unclasped his brass canister and smoothed the hand-drawn parchment across the wide stone railing. He retrieved his small stub of charcoal. With neat, steady strokes, he began adding his own journey to Barnaby's original sketch—marking the arch of Lookout Bridge, the spray of the fountain, and the towering silhouette of the Grand Library itself. Barnaby watched in silent delight, leaning in close before extending a gentle finger toward the southern horizon. "Cloudveil Ridge," the old clockmaker murmured warmly. "Where the afternoon clouds gather before they cross the valley."

James marked the distant mountains with a soft, wavy charcoal crest, blowing gently on the loose dust so the lines set clean. For the first time since leaving the Great Canopy, the map felt not merely like directions to follow, but a living record he was shaping with his own paws. Above them, deep within the tower's stone belly, the great bronze bells let out a single, sonorous hum that resonated down through the stone, vibrating gently through the soles of James's feet.
location: The Clock Tower Balcony, Grand Library, Oakhaven
